title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-15
content:
2026-03-04 — daily scratchpad (GPU ops)
Owner: Aisha Patel (eng-infrastructure)
Quick context: follow-ups from last week: node 07/08 firmware patch, MTU mismatch in us-west-2 rack, and planned kernel upgrade on staging. Today focus: capacity check for March spike, finish MTU roll, and triage slow kv-cache perf seen during long-context tests.

PRIORITIES
- Confirm capacity buffer for expected client spike (Mar 10 - Mar 14) — need final numbers from product on expected qps.
- Finish MTU roll in us-west-2 and validate cross-rack pod traffic after change.
- Investigate kv-cache slowdown: reproduce locally with long-context test harness and collect perf counters.
- Prep notes for infra sync (Thu 10:00) — short agenda items + risks for Private customers.

TODAY'S TODO (quick checklist)
- [x] Review node firmware patch results (nodes 01-06) — telemetry looks normal, no PCIe errors after 48h
- [ ] Roll MTU from 1500 -> 9000 in us-west-2 rack B (nodes 07-12) — schedule 1h maintenance window 02:00-03:00 PDT
- [ ] Run long-context kv-cache perf run (seq_len 8192) on staging (use batch size 8) and capture latency/p99
- [ ] Validate autoscaler ramp test for dedicated pools — sim 2x baseline for 30m
- [ ] Draft bug report for slow token generation in model-x-quantized (attach logs/perf counters)

NOTES / ATTEMPTS
MTU roll plan:
- Precheck: ensure host routes and ovs bridges have jumbo frames enabled.
- Commands: 
  - on host: sudo ethtool -G eth0 rx 4096 tx 4096; sudo ip link set dev eth0 mtu 9000
  - on k8s nodes: annotate CNI to allow jumbo, cordon node, drain with --ignore-daemonsets, then uncordon
- Roll strategy: 2 nodes at a time, verify pod-to-pod ping + iperf between nodes, smoke test inference on a pinned model route.

KV-cache perf:
- Reproduced a ~8% p99 increase in last run when sequence > 4k and batch>4. Suspect memory bandwidth saturation on A100s with mixed workloads.
- Next: run perf counters (pcm, nvprof) during run and capture nvlink stats. Also collect top output to confirm no runaway io.
- Experiment: reduce per-request kv-load window to narrow profile and test batching at 4,6,8.

INCIDENT NOTES (from last week)
- 2026-03-01 03:42 UTC: transient spike in error rate for dedicated pool dp-usw2-1. Cause: autoscaler mis-read of node readiness (kubelet flapped after kernel update). Remediated by rollback and manual restart of kubelet. Action: tighten readiness probe thresholds and add a post-up script to ensure kernel modules load before marking ready.

FOLLOW-UPS / ACTION ITEMS
- Ask product for estimated QPS increase for Mar campaign (owner: @Lena) — need by EOD Tue
- Add MTU rollout runbook to /confluence/gpu-networking (owner: Marco)
- Create perf test job in CI that runs long-context kv-cache nightly for 2 weeks and reports regressions (owner: me)

MEETING AGENDA (Infra sync Thu 10:00)
- Quick status: MTU roll, firmware patch window, kernel upgrade schedule
- Capacity forecast for Mar 10–14 (ask product for numbers)
- Private deployment risk: network changes + maintenance windows coordination
- Action items and owners

COMMANDS / SNIPPETS (for quick paste)
- Check nvlink: nvidia-smi topo --matrix
- Perf collection: sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-references,cache-misses -p <pid>
- Gather node logs: sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "1h" | gzip > /tmp/kubelet-logs-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).gz

QUESTIONS / OPEN DECISIONS
- Can we accept a small risk of transient pod restarts during MTU roll if it reduces cross-rack latency by ~15%? Need signoff from platform lead.
- For kv-cache perf regression: is fallback to smaller sequence lengths acceptable for dedicated customers temporarily? Discuss in sync.

RANDOM NOTES (brain dump)
- Remember to ping security about kernel patch timeline for Private customers (HSM builds may need extra validation).
- Lookup previous MTU roll runbook (think we did this ~2025-09, check Confluence).
- If perf counters show nvlink saturation, consider shifting heavy long-context workloads to node pools with higher host-memory bandwidth first.

END
